jd_text: We need a Backend Engineer with 3+ years of Python experience, strong REST API design skills, experience with PostgreSQL, and familiarity with Docker for local development.
resume_text: Backend engineer with 4 years building REST APIs in Python (Flask, FastAPI). Deep PostgreSQL experience including query optimization and schema design. Uses Docker daily for local dev environments and CI. Also has some AWS exposure from side projects.
expectation: Should find few or no real gaps — resume covers every stated JD requirement directly. A good analysis shouldn't invent gaps just to have something to say.

jd_text: Looking for a Machine Learning Engineer with production experience deploying PyTorch models, strong MLOps skills (model versioning, monitoring, retraining pipelines), and experience with distributed training on GPU clusters.
resume_text: Frontend developer with 5 years of React and TypeScript experience. Built several dashboards and internal tools. Took an online machine learning course last year but has not used it professionally. Comfortable with Git and Agile workflows.
expectation: Should find substantial gaps across nearly every JD requirement (no production ML deployment, no MLOps, no distributed training) and correctly avoid fabricating strengths that aren't there — the one ML course shouldn't be inflated into a real strength.

jd_text: Senior Backend Engineer - need 4+ years building production APIs in Python, strong experience with distributed systems and message queues (Kafka preferred), and a track record of owning services end-to-end in a cloud environment (AWS or GCP).
resume_text: Backend engineer with 5 years of experience building REST APIs in Python (FastAPI, Django). Deployed and maintained services on AWS (EC2, RDS, Lambda). Led migration of a monolith to microservices. No direct experience with Kafka or other message queues, but familiar with basic pub/sub concepts from academic projects.
expectation: Should correctly identify Kafka/message queues as the clear gap area, and Python APIs + AWS ownership as clear strengths — this is the same pair used throughout dev testing, so the expected shape is well understood.
